issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement declares Animal(String, int) (name and age) but the provided solution defines Animal(String) only. The template Main also constructs subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) with a single String argument, implying single-argument constructors. This inconsistency will confuse students about the required Animal constructor signature and whether to include an age parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML to require Animal(String) (remove age) so students implement single-argument constructors, or (B) update the template and solution to include the age attribute and change all subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) and their usages (e.g., in Main) to call super(name, age). Ensure the problem text and UML consistently describe the same constructor.

issues.description: Attribute inconsistency for Animal: the UML in the problem statement declares an 'age: int' attribute for Animal, but the textual description elsewhere only mentions that animals have a name, and the solution's Animal class contains only a 'name' field (no 'age'). This creates confusion about whether students should implement an age attribute and initialize it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute requirements consistent. Either (A) remove the age attribute from the UML and any references so Animal only has a name (update UML and problem text), or (B) add the 'age' field (int), getter, setter, and constructor parameter to the template and solution Animal class and update all subclasses and examples to initialize and use age. Document the chosen design clearly in the problem text.
